notes.title: Animus Non Grata - Special Edition is now available!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

The special edition of Animus Non Grata is finally available here on Steam! Game saves are [b]incompatible[/b] with the new version, meaning, a fresh save file is needed. If you wish to continue your adventure from an old save, the you need to use the "old twine version", which is bundled inside of the ANG-SE package. You can access it using the "Old Version (link)" in the game's main menu.

As always, let me know if there's bugs and typos! This is a complete re-write of the entire game, with dialogue and text modified to reflect the story-telling style delivered by Renpy.

- Special Edition is a Renpy remastered version of the game, written from scratch.
- Special Edition does not include Spanish translation
- Old 'Twine' version is still available in the game's installation folder. You can find it by pressing "Old Version (link)" in the main menu

notes.title: Animus Non Grata is back!
notes.notes: [p]Hey all,[/p][p][/p][p]I'm extremely sorry for the inconvenience experienced by you all when the game suddenly disappeared from Steam. I woke up one morning to an email saying the game had been retired (banned) without prior warning, and as such I failed to give you all a heads-up of what was going on. The game simply vanished from your libraries and was impossible to find on Steam, and it was completely out of my control.[/p][p][/p][p]These have been a rough couple of weeks, to say the least. Payment processors are deciding what kind to stories are allowed to be told, essentially choosing what "counts as real art" versus "content with no inherent artistic value". As a result of those tightened rules for adult games, Animus Non Grata was initially flagged for removal and was banned from Steam.[/p][p][/p][p]However, the fantastic staff over at Steam Support have reviewed the game's content and relisted the game! Clearly, the game's narrative and story-telling is strong enough to have artistic merit despite the dark subject matter.[/p][p][/p][p]I'm very glad for this decision and appreciate the opportunity to continue sharing this psychological horror thriller with you all here on Steam. However, the future is still unclear. Payment processors can decide at any point to make the rules even tighter, and force a ban on Animus Non Grata again. It's impossible to know what the future holds when it comes to censorship of free speech, video games and art.[/p][p][/p][p]What I can promise you is what I promised 2 month ago: I'll do my best to update this Steam page with the remastered Renpy-version "Special Edition" of Animus Non Grata. The original Twine edition is a well-written story, but the immersive format offered by Renpy should make the experience even better. I hope to bring the SE version to you as soon as possible.[/p][p][/p][p]Stay tuned for more news. And be careful out there.[/p][p][/p][p]Cheers,[/p][p]FlimsyLegs[/p]

notes.title: Animus Non Grata - Special Edition!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

I've started working on a full re-write of Animus Non Grata into Ren'Py, bringing the typical visual novel format into the game. Ren'Py is a popular visual novel engine and allows for creation of games that most people associate with visual novels. I have converted 4 out of 7 chapters at the time of writing, but due to summer vacation you'll have to wait until fall for a proper release!

This version is a "Special Edition". Game saves are INCOMPATIBLE between this version and the original Twine version of the game. I have to figure out the best way to bring you the special edition, while still allowing you to play the original version if you want to.

Stay tuned for the proper release announcement!

notes.title: Version 1.1.0 update - Spanish translation
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

For the past two months, I've been working with a professional translator [b]PrinDaisynha[/b], who has translated the entire game to Spanish! Proof-reading, beta-testing and correcting the Spanish translation was done by [b]Vicho75[/b]! The demo version also includes the Spanish translations.

In version 1.1.0, I needed to do major refactoring work to enable two languages to co-exist in a single Twine HTML project. You can choose your language in the beginning of the game and swap it whenever you like from the configuration menu. Your old game files should work without problems in this new version, and they default to English language when you load the save file. The translations have been tested only from new save game files, and this is the only officially supported way to play the translated (Spanish) version. However, there should be no technical reasons why loading an old save and changing the language to Spanish shouldn't work.

This update also includes some quality bug-fixes related to music when you load your saved game file, and adds a bit more image variety to the Thomas and Jack scenes in the backyard.

As always, let me know if you encounter bugs, and for the Spanish version, typos and such!

[strike]NOTE: Due to technical difficulties with steamworks and SYMLINKS, I've had to drop support for MacOS versions of this game. For now, all updates (including this v1.1.0 with the Spanish translation) will only be available on Windows. MacOS users will automatically download v1.0.2 of the game instead. I'm truly sorry for this issue and I will try to solve this issue![/strike]
UPDATE 2025.02.26: This issue has now been resolved and MacOS users can also download the latest v1.1.0 with the Spanish translation!

Cheers,
FlimsyLegs
[b]
Detailed v1.1.0 changelog:[/b]
[list]
[*] Increased image width from 90% to 100% of passage width
[*] Added Spanish translation for the entire game, by PrinDaisynha! NOTE: The translation works correctly only if you start a new save file. Loading an old save file and changing the language to Spanish may cause incorrect text to appear in some passages.
[*] Bugfix: Fix music bug in Sequence 0 caused by the "I believe you..." Passage when reached from the "You reach the kitchen" passage.
[*] Expanded image variety in Seq 3 scene with the boys in the yard (4 new images)
[*] Fixed music bug where two tracks played at the same time after loading a saved game
[*] Fixed music bug where the track would not play if the player loaded a save, until a "music change" passage was encountered
[/list]

notes.title: Boot sequence activated... Launching ANIMUS NON GRATA...!
notes.notes:
It's finally here, the launch day for Animus Non Grata! The game is now available for download on Steam! If you encounter bugs, please let me know in the community hub or in the game's discord server!

[i]Are you ready to step into the shoes on an AI android is a harsh world, fighting against or embracing your programming?[/i]

Cheers,
FlimsyLegs

[b]PS: Below is a bit of insight into the background and inspiration for the game:[/b]

The story of Animus Non Grata is heavily inspired by “Westworld” and “Ex Machina”, and to a lesser extent “Her”. Being a heavy metal fan, the songs “Colossus” by Avatar and “AI” by Raubtier were the ones that finally kicked off the creative process. I wanted the story of Animus Non Grata to be a rollercoaster of emotions, a tale that sticks with the player, and hopefully makes them question the rapid rise of AI in everything around us.

We see artificial intelligence popping up everywhere, like those with the capabilities to navigate the environment (autonomous vehicles, robots). There’s large language models that seem intelligent and can fetch information from other websites to enhance their answers (a process known as retrieval augmented generation). We have computer vision, where a computer can “see” the world around them.

The one thing common about AI today is that they are built for a very narrow set of tasks. It doesn’t take a lot of searching online to find countless of incidents of AI-related issues, from fast food chain's ordering AI adding 260 chicken nuggets to an order, to autonomous vehicles not recognizing pedestrians from trees.

In other words, AI is bad at operating outside their programmed and trained scenarios. We are expanding those scenarios with better training data, but still today the AI will essentially perform “unknowable” operations on situations that it hasn’t encountered before.

However, thankfully we are still far away from artificial general intelligence, which has been predicted to be everything from the end of humanity, to simply being an extremely tricky moral conundrum. What are the rights of an AGI? Should it be considered a free entity, or is it just a fancy computer?

To tie it all back to the story of Animus Non Grata: We have websites offering AI girlfriends to people popping up by the dozen already, and human-like robots being created even today. Outside the realm of technology we have blow-up dolls, which in 2023 was a 6835 million dollar industry. Combine all of those things, and you get the dystopian premise of Animus Non Grata, where you get to see a harsh world from the surreal perspective of an AI android.
